title: Majestic Pawn: Remove Every Restraint
summary: Offer both queens and the bishop to release a pinned pawn, while checking the blocks that can decline each sacrifice.

nodes.question: Why is the g-pawn unable to move, and how can White free it?
nodes.explanation: Rg1 pins g4 against Kh4, while Rd4 attacks along the fourth rank. Qc1+ lures one rook away, Bd2+ lures the other, and Qf4+ draws the knight onto f4 before g5 mate.

branches.title: Source plan: two queens and a bishop
commentary: Begin after ...Bg6. White has two queens, but the g4 pawn is pinned on the g-file and cannot yet check the king.
Qc1+ checks along c1–d2–e3–f4–g5–h6. The queen is offered to the rook on g1, with the aim of breaking the pawn’s pin.
Rxc1 accepts that queen. The rook leaves the g-file, so g4 is no longer pinned against Kh4, but Rd4 still controls the fourth rank.
Bd2+ checks along d2–e3–f4–g5–h6. This second offer places the bishop where Rd4 can capture it.
Rxd2 accepts the bishop and clears the fourth rank. The pawn can move without uncovering a rook attack on White’s king.
Qf4+ checks along f4–g5–h6 and offers the remaining queen to Nh3. White is preparing the pawn’s final advance.
Nxf4 accepts the queen. Black’s knight now occupies f4, while g5 is free for White’s pawn.
g5# checks Kh6. Kh4 protects g5 and h5; the pawn checks h6, Bg6 blocks g6, Qg7 blocks g7, h7 blocks h7, and the king cannot capture the protected pawn or interpose against its adjacent check.
branches.explanation: g5# checks Kh6. Kh4 protects g5 and h5; the pawn checks h6, Bg6 blocks g6, Qg7 blocks g7, h7 blocks h7, and the king cannot capture the protected pawn or interpose against its adjacent check.

branches.title: Independent defense: block immediately on g5
commentary: Black can decline the queen capture by blocking the checking diagonal with the knight.
Qc1+ starts the same diagonal check and keeps White’s mating strategy.
Ng5 interposes the knight on the diagonal from c1 to h6. It is legal, but the knight lands on a square protected by Kh4.
Qxg5# captures that blocker with Qc1. Kh4 protects the queen on g5; the queen controls g6 and h5, and Black’s own pieces and pawn occupy the upper flights.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qxg5# captures that blocker with Qc1. Kh4 protects the queen on g5; the queen controls g6 and h5, and Black’s own pieces and pawn occupy the upper flights.

branches.title: Independent defense: block with the rook on d2
commentary: The rook on d4 may block the first diagonal check instead of waiting for the bishop offer.
Qc1+ checks along the long diagonal toward h6.
Rd2 interposes the rook on d2, leaving the rook on g1 in place. White must answer the actual block rather than replay the source capture order.
Bxd2+ removes the block with check. The bishop from b4 now joins the attack along the same diagonal.
Nf4 interposes the knight. Ng5 is the other legal defense here and also loses, as saved in the complete proof.
Qxf4# captures the knight with Qc1. The queen checks h6 along the diagonal and closes the remaining flights. Black cannot restore the captured block.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qxf4# captures the knight with Qc1. The queen checks h6 along the diagonal and closes the remaining flights. Black cannot restore the captured block.

branches.title: Independent defense: block on f4 first
commentary: The other initial knight block goes to f4 rather than g5. Both queens have access to that square.
Qc1+ checks h6 along the diagonal.
Nf4 interposes on the checking diagonal, while also occupying the fourth rank.
Qfxf4+ uses the queen from f8 to capture the knight. The file letter distinguishes it from the queen on c1, which can also capture f4.
Rxf4 takes that queen with Rd4. It is the only legal response to the renewed check.
Qxf4# captures the rook with the queen from c1. The bishop still on b4 and White’s king/pawn support the mating net.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qxf4# captures the rook with the queen from c1. The bishop still on b4 and White’s king/pawn support the mating net.

branches.title: Independent defense: block with the rook on f4
commentary: Black’s fifth initial reply uses the rook to interpose directly on f4.
Qc1+ is the proved first check.
Rf4 blocks the c1–h6 diagonal and offers the rook instead of taking the queen on c1.
Qfxf4+ captures that rook with the queen from f8. White chooses which queen to offer so the other remains ready to recapture.
Nxf4 accepts the queen with Nh3. Ng5 is also legal and is included in the complete proof; White can capture it with mate.
Qxf4# uses the queen on c1 to capture the knight and finish the diagonal mate. The preserved black bishop, queen and h-pawn help confine their own king.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Qxf4# uses the queen on c1 to capture the knight and finish the diagonal mate. The preserved black bishop, queen and h-pawn help confine their own king.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t White just push g5 in the starting diagram?
exercises.answer: Rg1 pins the g4 pawn to Kh4. Moving it would expose White’s king to check.

exercises.prompt: Does the proof assume Black takes every sacrifice?
exercises.answer: No. It enumerates all five replies to Qc1+, all four replies to Bd2+ after Rxc1, and both knight replies to the final queen offer.
